item.title: Drill 2026-10-24: decode one instruction
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64.
Decode this instruction, located at address `0x140001000`:
``` 0F 8C 2A 01 00 00 ```
What is the assembly (give the absolute target address)? Why is this two opcode bytes, and when would a compiler use a 2-byte form instead?
---
## Answer
`jl 0x140001130` (jump if less, signed).
- `0F` is the two-byte opcode escape; `0F 8C` = JL rel32 (near conditional jump; 0F 8x mirrors the short `7x` forms, so `7C` = JL rel8). Condition is SF != OF, i.e. signed less-than after a cmp. - Displacement `2A 01 00 00` little-endian = 0x0000012A, signed, relative to the NEXT instruction: 0x140001000 + 6 = 0x140001006; + 0x12A = 0x140001130. - Compilers emit the 2-byte `7C rel8` when the target is within -128..+127 bytes; otherwise they need this 6-byte rel32 form.
